messages:
Maria (sales-engineer): Heads up — ACME procurement flagged a discrepancy: AWS Marketplace charges are showing as 'Redwood API' while our direct invoice lists reserved commit line items. They want a single PO that covers marketplace + direct. Any known pattern to map marketplace SKUs to our rate card?
Andrew (sales-ops): We saw this with BetaCorp. Marketplace and direct flows are different entities. Short answer: either a Private Offer (marketplace-side) or a mapping doc we attach to invoices. Which ACME legal/entity?
Maria (sales-engineer): ACME US (ACME, Inc). Procurement needs PO line items to match: product, SKU, unit price, qty. Also want net vs gross and tax breakdown visible on invoice.
Kevin (finance): Finance note — marketplace settlements are net-of-marketplace fees. Customer PO can reference Marketplace Order ID; we can provide a mapping file that reconciles MP orders to our direct commit invoices. If they want consolidated formatting, deal-desk + legal signoff likely required.
Liz (deal-desk): If they want a unified invoice we can offer managed billing (consolidation) but it requires cross-team approvals. Pricing itself shouldn't change, but marketplace fee passthrough and settlement timing do matter.
Maria (sales-engineer): Do we have a short mapping example I can send procurement? They asked for a sample single-invoice with how credits/commit offsets appear.
billing-bot: FYI docs: https://redwood.example/docs/marketplace-invoicing-mapping (public link)
Andrew (sales-ops): Quick sample snippet for procurement (feel free to copy):
```
Marketplace order: MP-789012
Redwood SKU (marketplace line): RED-API-XS
Marketplace unit price: $0.0009 / token
Direct commit SKU (our invoice): RED-DED-XS
Commit unit price: $0.00085 / token
Mapping rule: MP-789012 -> RED-DED-XS (commit applied as credit on monthly invoice)
```
Andrew (sales-ops): I'm going to escalate to deal-desk. @Liz can you start the approval path? Please loop in Legal if necessary.
Liz (deal-desk): Will do. Need from Maria: customer PO PDF, expected monthly spend, term length, whether they want a Private Offer, and the requested billing entity. Also note any requested invoice fields/format.
Kevin (finance): Also send customer tax ID and whether the PO is gross or net. If they insist on a single consolidated invoice that spans marketplace & direct charges, timeline will be longer (coordination + marketplace contract adjustments).
Maria (sales-engineer): Got it — pinging ACME procurement for PO + tax info and whether they'll accept a mapping attachment as interim. Will share reply here.
Andrew (sales-ops): If they need a short-term workaround, we can issue both invoices and include a reconciliation table (Marketplace order -> Redwood invoice line) while approvals happen.
Maria (sales-engineer): Perfect, thanks. I'll update when I hear back. :thumbsup:
Liz (deal-desk): Thanks — starting the internal SR.
Kevin (finance): Thanks all.
